function.name: EventSettingsApi_create_website_alert_config
function.description: Creates a configuration for website alerting within the system, allowing users to define conditions under which alerts should be triggered for a website. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name for the website alert configuration.

description.description: A detailed description for the website alert configuration.

severity.description: The severity level of the alert when triggered.

triggering.description: Flag indicating whether the alert configuration should also trigger an incident.

websiteId.description: The unique identifier of the website for which the alert configuration is created.

tagFilterExpression.description: A boolean expression used to filter the scope of website beacons based on tags.

granularity.description: The evaluation granularity in seconds used for detection of threshold violations.

rule.description: The type of rule this alert configuration pertains to, such as 'traffic spike' or 'downtime'.

threshold.description: The threshold value that, when exceeded, will trigger the alert. This is a float type value.

timeThreshold.description: The time duration in seconds during which the threshold must be exceeded to trigger the alert.

alertChannelIds.description: A list of alert channel IDs defined in Instana to which the alert notifications will be sent.

Instana’s public REST‑API is organized into **major “v” namespaces** – the most recent stable release at the moment is **`/api/v2/*`**.  
Below is a quick snapshot of what each namespace represents:

| Namespace | Status | Typical Base URL | Notes |
|-----------|--------|------------------|-------|
| `/api/v1/*` | Legacy / deprecated | `https://<instana-host>/api/v1/...` | Still available for backward compatibility, but new features and bug fixes are only added to v2. |
| `/api/v2/*` | Current production | `https://<instana-host>/api/v2/...` | All modern SDKs, dashboards, and automation scripts target this endpoint set. |

### How to confirm your instance’s active API version

If you’re unsure which version your environment exposes, simply try hitting one of the following health checks:

```bash
curl -u <username>:<password> https://<your-instana>.com/api/v2/status
```

or, if you prefer the legacy path:

```bash
curl -u <username>:<password> https://<your-instana>.com/api/v1/status
```

A successful response (`200 OK`) indicates that the corresponding namespace is enabled. In practice, almost all newer installations expose both paths, but the *recommended* way forward is always through `/api/v2`.

---

#### Quick reference for common v2 endpoints

| Feature | Endpoint pattern | Example |
|---------|-------------------|---------|
| List services | `GET /services` | `GET https://…/api/v2/services` |
| Create alert config | `POST /alerts/configurations` | `POST https://…/api/v2/alerts/configurations` |
| Fetch metrics | `GET /metrics/{metricName}` | `GET https://…/api/v2/metrics/cpu.utilization` |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper examples—e.g., constructing a specific request body for creating an alert or querying metric data over a custom time window!
